verses.text: For three years there was no war between Syria and Israel.
In the third year, Jehoshaphat king of Judah went down to visit the king of Israel.
The king of Israel said to his officials, "You know that Ramoth Gilead belongs to us. So why are we doing nothing to take it back from the king of Syria?"
He asked Jehoshaphat, "Will you go with me to fight at Ramoth Gilead?" Jehoshaphat answered the king of Israel, "I am with you all the way. My people are your people, and my horses are your horses."
But Jehoshaphat also said to the king of Israel, "First, please ask what the LORD says."

So the king of Israel gathered the prophets, about four hundred men, and asked them, "Should I go to war against Ramoth Gilead, or should I hold back?" They answered, "Go, because the Lord will hand it over to the king."
But Jehoshaphat asked, "Is there not a prophet of the LORD here whom we can ask?"

The king of Israel answered Jehoshaphat, "There is still one man through whom we can ask the LORD. He is Micaiah son of Imlah. But I hate him, because he never says anything good about me, only bad." Jehoshaphat said, "The king should not say that."
So the king of Israel called one of his officials and said, "Bring Micaiah son of Imlah at once."

The king of Israel and Jehoshaphat king of Judah were dressed in their royal robes, sitting on their thrones at the threshing floor by the entrance to the gate of Samaria. All the prophets were prophesying in front of them.
Zedekiah son of Kenaanah had made iron horns. He said, "This is what the LORD says: 'With these you will gore the Syrians until they are destroyed.'"
All the other prophets said the same thing: "Attack Ramoth Gilead and win, because the LORD will hand it over to the king."
The messenger who had gone to get Micaiah said to him, "Look, all the other prophets agree and are saying good things to the king. Please let your message agree with theirs, and say something good."
But Micaiah said, "As surely as the LORD lives, I will say only what the LORD tells me."

When he came to the king, the king asked him, "Micaiah, should we go to war against Ramoth Gilead, or should we hold back?" Micaiah answered, "Go and win, because the LORD will hand it over to the king."
The king said to him, "How many times must I make you promise to tell me nothing but the truth in the LORD's name?"
Then Micaiah said, "I saw all Israel scattered on the hills like sheep without a shepherd. And the LORD said, 'These people have no master. Let each one go home in peace.'"
The king of Israel said to Jehoshaphat, "Didn't I tell you that he never says anything good about me, only bad?"
Micaiah went on, "So listen to the LORD's word. I saw the LORD sitting on his throne, with all the armies of heaven standing around him, on his right and on his left.
The LORD said, 'Who will trick Ahab into attacking Ramoth Gilead, so he will die there?' One said one thing, and another said something else.
Then a spirit came forward, stood before the LORD, and said, 'I will trick him.'
The LORD asked, 'How?' The spirit said, 'I will go out and be a lying spirit in the mouths of all his prophets.' The LORD said, 'You will trick him, and you will succeed. Go and do it.'
So now, the LORD has put a lying spirit in the mouths of all these prophets of yours. The LORD has decided to bring disaster on you."
Then Zedekiah son of Kenaanah walked up and slapped Micaiah in the face. He said, "Which way did the LORD's Spirit go when he left me to speak to you?"
Micaiah answered, "You will find out on the day you go and hide in an inner room."
The king of Israel said, "Take Micaiah and send him back to Amon the governor of the city and to Joash the king's son.
Tell them, 'This is what the king says: Put this man in prison and give him nothing but a little bread and water until I come back safely.'"
Micaiah said, "If you ever come back safely, then the LORD has not spoken through me." Then he added, "Listen to this, all you people!"
So the king of Israel and Jehoshaphat king of Judah went up to Ramoth Gilead.
The king of Israel said to Jehoshaphat, "I will disguise myself and go into battle, but you wear your royal robes." So the king of Israel disguised himself and went into battle.
The king of Syria had ordered his thirty-two chariot commanders, "Do not fight anyone, small or great, except the king of Israel."
When the chariot commanders saw Jehoshaphat, they thought, "That must be the king of Israel!" So they turned to attack him. But Jehoshaphat cried out.
When the chariot commanders saw that he was not the king of Israel, they stopped chasing him.

But someone shot an arrow without aiming, and it hit the king of Israel between the pieces of his armour. The king told his chariot driver, "Turn around and get me out of the battle. I am badly wounded."
The battle raged all day long. The king was propped up in his chariot facing the Syrians, and he died that evening. The blood from his wound ran down onto the floor of the chariot.
As the sun was setting, a shout went through the army: "Every man back to his own town! Every man back to his own land!"
So the king died, and he was brought to Samaria and buried there.
They washed his chariot at the pool of Samaria, where the prostitutes bathed, and dogs licked up his blood, just as the LORD had said.
The rest of what Ahab did, all his deeds, the ivory palace he built, and all the towns he built, are written in the book of the history of the kings of Israel.
Ahab died, and his son Ahaziah became king after him.
Jehoshaphat son of Asa became king of Judah in the fourth year that Ahab was king of Israel.
Jehoshaphat was thirty-five years old when he became king, and he ruled in Jerusalem for twenty-five years. His mother was Azubah, the daughter of Shilhi.

He followed all the ways of his father Asa and did not turn away from them. He did what was right in the LORD's eyes. But the high places were not removed, and the people still offered sacrifices and burned incense there.
Jehoshaphat also made peace with the king of Israel.
The rest of what Jehoshaphat did, the power he showed, and the wars he fought, are written in the book of the history of the kings of Judah.
He drove out of the land the rest of the male shrine prostitutes who were still there from the time of his father Asa.
At that time there was no king in Edom. A governor ruled there.
Jehoshaphat built large trading ships to sail to Ophir for gold. But they never sailed, because they were wrecked at Ezion Geber.
Then Ahaziah son of Ahab said to Jehoshaphat, "Let my sailors go with your sailors on the ships." But Jehoshaphat refused.
Jehoshaphat died and was buried with his ancestors in the city of his ancestor David. His son Jehoram became king after him.
Ahaziah son of Ahab became king of Israel in Samaria in the seventeenth year that Jehoshaphat was king of Judah. He ruled Israel for two years.
He did what was evil in the LORD's eyes. He followed the ways of his father and mother, and the ways of Jeroboam son of Nebat, who made Israel sin.
He served Baal and worshipped him. He made the LORD, the God of Israel, angry, just as his father had done.
